doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Trios, electric questions and the big band
title: Recasting 'Fly With the Wind' and 'Passion Dance' for big band
summary: Tyner says he likes hearing his music in new settings, and they recall Billy Cobham and Cal Massey's big band.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So rehearsing, you had a conductor, but that may have been just for the recording. I don’t recall seeing a conductor when you came through, you were leading the band.
Yeah that was for recording, right.

So now, what made this especially gratifying for me is I heard all those big band projects, “Fly With the Wind”, “Song For the New World”, but to see it performed live-because you do “Fly With the Wind” on here. “Passion Dance” which was originally, that’s why I

wanted to bring up the quartet first with Joe Henderson, now expanded for a big band, so again to me this is demonstrating this continual growth. Even though you’re re-visiting older material, or previous material, it’s recast now, it’s now reflecting your sensibility at this stage in your life.

Yeah, well see I never felt like I shouldn’t record my own music in a different setting. I wanted to hear it with a big band, “Fly with the Wind” I did an arrangement with a band. “Fly with the Wind” I had originally done it for strings. So I think it’s good, you learn about other instrumentation. I like the string version of “Fly with the Wind” too.
I remember because I remember Billy Cobham played on that too and he was playing like the wind. He was playing like the wind on that one!
Yes, that’s right! Yeah, they did things on Inner Voices but he did it at Carnegie years ago with him and Bill [inaudible]. But I love big bands.
I like big bands. Maybe it’s because I was around Cal Massey when I was young.
She was a great singer, she was in Cal Massey’s band. Growing up in Philly was really a great experience, it really was.
